It's really frustrating when the people who are supposed to help don't seem to get it. Your experience is valid — many autistic people find that traditional CBT isn't a good fit, and that's not a failure on your part. The mismatch is real.

You might have better luck seeking out neurodiversity-affirming therapists who specifically understand autistic experiences. Occupational therapists can also help with sensory regulation strategies. In the meantime, learning your personal triggers and early warning signs can help you prepare — things like noise-canceling headphones, weighted items, or having a quiet exit plan can make a difference.

Online autistic communities can be valuable for practical tips from people who actually live this. Organizations like ASAN offer resources written by autistic people. You deserve support that actually fits how your brain works.
